newsitem.title: BRAZIL: FOCUS-Brazil crosses fingers, hopes for CVRD sale.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Brazil crosses fingers, hopes for CVRD sale.

text.p: Brazil Tuesday appealed to bidders to turn up for the scheduled auction of mining giant Companhia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD) and said it was optimistic it could defeat a host of legal challenges to the sale.

"I am confident we will be able to quash these injunctions," said Luiz Carlos Mendonca de Barros, head of the National Development Bank (BNDES), saying that of nine injunctions issued Monday only four remained to be overturned.
"Some of these injunctions don't make any sense," Mendonca de Barros told Globo television in a an interview.

A small army of government lawyers spent all night fighting law suits in courts across the country in order to ensure the $2.8 billion sale of 45 percent of CVRD's voting shares could begin as planned at 1000 local/1300 GMT.

The BNDES, which runs Brazil's privatization program, has given itself until 1700 local/2000 GMT to get the bidding underway. Otherwise, officials acknowledge Latin America's biggest planned privatization to date will have to be suspended.
Late on Monday night, police in Rio de Janeiro forcefully dispersed about 100 protesters trying to camp outside the bolsa where the auction was due to take place.
Local media said the police used stun grenades and tear gas as well as wading in with batons.
Globo newspaper said six people were injured, including one police officer struck by a stone.

Trade union leaders and opponents of the sale, ranging from former presidents to all the country's Catholic bishops, have vowed to bring at least 5,000 people in for a protest at the stock exchange Tuesday.
But by early morning only a few demonstrators had gathered near the square in front of the exchange, which had been ringed off by high fences and riot police.

The privatization of CVRD, the world's largest iron ore exporter, should raise at least $5.0 billion for the government's coffers once completed and thus qualify as the biggest Latin American state sell-off ever.

CVRD's Carajas mine, deep in the Amazon, holds the world's largest iron ore deposit estimated at 18 billion tonnes. The group, which enjoys a rare public sector reputation for efficiency, also mines copper, gold and manganese.
Two multinational consortia were in the bidding for the 45 percent stake going under the hammer on Tuesday.
One was being led by Brazilian steelmaker CSN and the other by local pulp, cement and metal concern Votorantim together with South Africa's Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd.
